Karthik,

They asked for a view they can give their SRE and finance teams to reconcile usage spikes. Can you confirm whether we can deliver a minimal per-route breakdown tile in the Console for the April sprint?

Ask:
- Per-route cost/time-series (1h, 24h, 7d windows)
- Alert if a route's unit-cost increases >25% vs baseline
- CSV export of raw attribution (they want a sample for procurement)

I've attached a small sample export they sent us (route_cost_sample.csv) and pasted their ask at the bottom of this thread. Ideally we ship a light-weight explorer tile + an export button; we can expand later.

Timeline: Acme is aiming to run the pilot starting Apr 20 — so we need an internal cut by Apr 15 to QA.

Thanks — Marissa

Subject: Re: Route economics: Acme pilot — sprint integration checklist

Marissa — thanks for the context. High-level plan:

1) Data: we can compute per-route token counts + model variant CPU/GPU multipliers; the trick is attributing shared cache hits and batching overhead. For an MVP I propose we use sampled-attribution at the request-path level (1 in 20) and extrapolate. That will give the CSV they want and keep query cost modest.

2) Console UI: a compact "Route Economics" tile that shows a sparkline for cost per minute, median tail latency, and a three-dot menu with "Export CSV". Backend: new aggregation job + S3/BigQuery dump for export.

3) Alerts: simple rule engine — we can wire the existing alert infra to trigger when unit-cost delta > 25% compared to a 7d rolling baseline.

Constraints: sampling adds +/- 3–6% variance on small routes; we'll note that in the CSV metadata. Also need product signoff on the UI (Lauren) and a small privacy check if Acme requests per-user breakdowns (they said no, but we should confirm).

Can you confirm Acme is OK with sampling and the Apr 15 internal cut? If yes I'll stub the aggregation job and push a mock Console tile for review by Apr 12.

—Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>

Thanks — looped in product and UX. A couple of product constraints and suggestions for the MVP:

- MVP scope: aggregation + export + one Console tile. No deep drilldowns or per-tenant overlays in this sprint. We can mark exploratory drilldowns as "phase 2".
- UX: prefer a single-time-range selector tied to Console (1h/24h/7d) and a toggle for "show raw samples". The attached sketch is a low-fidelity for the tile (console-widget-sketch.png).
- Compliance: Acme confirmed they don't need PII attribution. Still, run the export pipeline through Security for a quick review.

Acceptance criteria for Apr 15 internal cut:
- Aggregation job completes for last 7 days of sandbox traffic
- Tile shows cost-per-minute + p95 latency for selected routes
- CSV export includes sampling rate and extrapolation notes
- Alert rule exists and triggers in staging for injected anomaly

I'll prioritize a small UX pass and will add the Console ticket to the April sprint board (HS-342112). Karthik, if you can drop a staging demo link by Apr 12 we'll review with Sales next week.

—Lauren
